item.title: [EN|In-Depth] BBC Global News Podcast (Sat 14:00): The Happy Pod: The choir proud to admit they can't sing
item.description:
Originally published Sat 12 Sep 2026 14:00 IDT.

The Off-Key Choir in Southport on Merseyside has a simple motto: just because you can't sing doesn't mean you shouldn't. Around 80 members come together every week to sing their hearts out, without the pressure to hit all the right notes. Since it was formed in 2018, the choir has also acted as a support group. It has become so popular there is now a waiting list to join.

Also: the successful canopy bridge project giving animals a safe way to cross roads in the vast Amazon rainforest. How a pirate ship themed video game is helping stroke survivors in Mexico to regain mobility. A pilot scheme from Guide Dogs is turning ultrasound scans into 3D printed models for expectant parents with sight loss to feel their unborn baby's features. Campaigners across Africa are celebrating after a UN vote to adopt a new world map reflecting the true size of the continent. Plus, as a new Gruffalo book is released, we hear why the original story resonates with so many children.

(Image: Sheila Byrne, member of the Off-Key Choir. Credit: BBC)

Presenter: Chantal Hartle. Music: Iona Hampson
